DRB enables dynamic reasoning budget allocation across five frontier models and three datasets, matching or improving F1 over always-maximum-budget baselines in 9/15 settings while reducing cost, and shows preliminary promise for cross-model selection generalization.
stories_overflow.why_it_matters: It offers a practical path to compute-optimal, layout-aware reasoning allocation and model selection for document tasks, directly relevant to secure and efficient deployment of reasoning LLMs.
stories_overflow.reason: A lightweight multimodal estimator to predict LLM reasoning performance (compute-budget tradeoffs) is useful for compute-optimal allocation and efficient red-teaming at scale, relevant to security/serving tradeoffs.

stories_overflow.title: DreamGuard: Efficient Runtime Guardrail for LLM Agents via Risk-Aware World Model
stories_overflow.summary: DreamGuard is a proactive runtime guardrail for LLM agents that uses a risk-aware world model to track a compact recurrent latent state over trajectories and forecast future latent states. From these forecasts, it derives immediate-hazard and prefix-risk evidence and fuses multi-horizon signals to decide on interventions before tool executions. Across four benchmarks and an online evaluation, DreamGuard outperforms generic, reactive, and proactive baselines with the best safety-utility trade-off and averages 25 ms end-to-end latency per call.
stories_overflow.why_it_matters: Introduces a trajectory-aware, low-latency guardrail with explicit risk modeling, aligning with interests in long-horizon safety for LLM agents and bridging to sequence modeling ideas from time series foundation models.
stories_overflow.reason: Adaptive allocation across model populations for LLM-driven evolutionary search is relevant for cost-efficient red-teaming/evolutionary program search, but more about budgeting than core security.

stories_overflow.title: SkillTFM: Gated Skill Evolution for Training-Free Adaptation of Tabular Foundation Models
stories_overflow.summary: The paper introduces SkillTFM, a training-free adaptation system for tabular foundation models that replaces parameter updates with gated evolution of agentic skills. It uses a verifiable, extensible skill bank combining boundary evidence identification to characterize task structure and base-model failures with gated skill evolution to retrieve and extend reusable skills under explicit validation. In simulated boundary settings and real-world electricity-price forecasting, SkillTFM improves AUC by 0.128–0.142, elevating nonlinear-boundary AUC from 0.699 to 0.898, and shows effectiveness across different TFM backbones.
stories_overflow.why_it_matters: It proposes a security-adjacent, verifiable skill-gating mechanism for training-free adaptation under distribution shift, echoing modular skill libraries and guarded tool-use in LLMs while targeting tabular/time-series TFMs.
stories_overflow.reason: Empirical study of self-pretraining for medical time series—useful data on pretraining benefits and transfer in noisy, multimodal TS settings though domain-specific.

stories_overflow.title: Learning the Pareto Frontier of Predictive Models under Distribution Shift
stories_overflow.summary: The paper introduces Frontier Learning, which treats a library of pretrained models with mixed access regimes (black-box predictions and white-box representations) as complementary sources under distribution shift. It builds a unified target-domain feature by concatenating internal representations from white-box models with outputs from black-box models, then trains a lightweight regularized supervised learner, guaranteeing training-sample risk no worse than any single baseline including zero-shot reuse, fine-tuning, or direct training. Experiments on simulations and real-world shifts (DomainNet/VisDA and MIMIC-IV-Notes ICU mortality) show it matches or outperforms the strongest individual reuse strategy, with the largest gains when no single baseline is reliable across the shifts considered.
stories_overflow.why_it_matters: Provides a simple, access-agnostic ensemble-on-representations approach that subsumes common reuse strategies and is empirically strong under shift—relevant to robustness/security and modular reuse of foundation models.
stories_overflow.reason: Agentic BO using LLMs to inject priors into optimization touches on agentic systems and leveraging LLMs as components—relevant to attack/defense surfaces and efficient automated red-teaming workflows.

stories_overflow.title: LabelFusion-TS: Fusing Large Language Models, Transformer Encoders, and Financial Time Series for Monetary-Policy Stance Classification
stories_overflow.summary: The paper introduces LabelFusion-TS, which combines a fine-tuned RoBERTa encoder, a prompted LLM, and an ensemble of time-series transformers over pre-publication market series via a small voting network to classify FOMC sentences as hawkish, dovish, or neutral. Due to limited human labels (~1k sentences), the RoBERTa encoder is first pre-trained on LLM-generated weak labels and then fine-tuned on human annotations. Trained on data up to 2015 and evaluated on 2015–2022, the fused system attains 70.2% weighted F1, surpassing a zero-shot LLM at 64.1% and overtaking it with as few as 240 human-labeled sentences.
stories_overflow.why_it_matters: It demonstrates measurable gains from fusing market time series with LLM/text encoders for monetary-policy stance classification, highlighting a practical multimodal path beyond text-only classifiers.
stories_overflow.reason: Multimodal fusion of financial time series with LLMs for stance classification touches the reader's TSFM interest (benchmarks/architectures) and evaluation, though it's a narrow financial NLP application.

stories_overflow.title: Analysis of Federated Aggregation under Model Poisoning and Backdoor Attacks: A Reconstructed Cross-Dataset and Cross-Architecture Benchmark
stories_overflow.summary: This work reconstructs a 500-cell federated aggregation benchmark across five methods, five datasets, five architectures, and four conditions (clean, sign-flipping, Gaussian, BadNets), recovering 454 original runs and 36 repairs/reruns, with 10 SVHN cells covered only by summary provenance. Trimmed Mean has the best clean macro-mean accuracy and lowest mean within-task rank, while Krum shows the top recorded accuracy under sign-flipping and Gaussian, and these rankings persist when restricted to fully logged task pairs. Audits reveal the BadNets metric is actually TTLR (all test inputs triggered) and a FedPARETO pathway where reported predictive summaries may not match the corrupted updates used for aggregation, so results are descriptive within recorded configs rather than universal robustness claims.
stories_overflow.why_it_matters: Highlights reproducibility gaps, metric mis-specification (TTLR), and aggregation/provenance pitfalls that can confound robustness claims in federated settings relevant to secure FL and poisoning/backdoor evaluation.
stories_overflow.reason: Cross‑dataset benchmark for federated aggregation under poisoning/backdoors informs robust evaluation and threat models though it's more federated learning than LLM‑specific.

stories_overflow.title: Into the ORBIT for Time Series: Training Regimes for Foundation Models
stories_overflow.summary: The paper introduces ORBIT, a training paradigm for TSFMs that explicitly controls pre-training distributions via Bootstrap Multi-Level Sampling and Omni-Range Incremental Training. It trains Falcon-2.0, a univariate encoder-only Transformer with missingness-aware triple-channel patch tokenization and parallel patch prediction, under this regime. The authors also propose Rank-Guided Cross-Depth Alignment to align shallow and deep representations, and report strong zero-shot forecasting on GIFT-Eval and fev-bench across diverse domains and frequencies.
stories_overflow.why_it_matters: It provides a principled, controllable pretraining regime and lightweight representation alignment that could transfer to secure LLM pretraining curricula and to robust TSFM deployment across heterogeneous, imbalanced time-series corpora.
stories_overflow.reason: Evaluation metric for synthetic limit-order-book time series is relevant for TSFM evaluation and assessing generative-model fidelity, with potential security implications for market-simulation attacks.

stories_overflow.title: Revisiting WEASEL 2.0: Reproduction, Sensitivity, and an Adaptive Ensemble-Size Rule
stories_overflow.summary: The paper reproduces WEASEL 2.0 on 114 UCR datasets, matching reported accuracy (mean 0.865, median 0.928; Wilcoxon p = 0.655). It probes sensitivity of four design choices, finding the downstream classifier, lack of feature weighting, and the max window-size rule to be robust, while the fixed max ensemble-size rule is over-provisioned for long series. An adaptive rule based on series length and number of classes cuts peak fit memory and time on fixed-length datasets with essentially no median accuracy change.
stories_overflow.why_it_matters: Offers a principled, resource-saving ensemble-size heuristic for dictionary TSC that preserves accuracy—useful for scaling long-sequence models and benchmarking efficient TS foundations.
stories_overflow.reason: Reproduction and sensitivity analysis of a time-series classifier (WEASEL 2.0) is directly relevant to TSFM benchmarking and methodological rigor, but it's a classical classifier rather than a foundation-model pretraining advance.

stories_overflow.title: Feature Priming in Online Linear Regression: Sparse-Regret Lower Bounds and a Tight Univariate Rate
stories_overflow.summary: The paper studies feature priming for high-dimensional online linear regression and answers a COLT 2023 question negatively for three Moore–Penrose priming rules, showing sparse-logarithmic regret is impossible under a natural past-data protocol. It identifies nuisance interpolation as the mechanism that underweights the predictive coordinate and proves Ω(min{T, sqrt(d)}) regret via Hadamard-style constructions, even against a zero-loss one-sparse comparator, with variants for prime powers and rule selection. On the positive side, it shows regret controlled by data rank and matches this with a Euclidean-normalized triangular lower bound for powered univariate priming (robust to nonnegative ridge), plus a paired ridge construction covering all three powered rules, and reports diagnostics on frozen LM activations reflecting the same failure mode; multivariate and Pearson frontiers remain open.
stories_overflow.why_it_matters: Clarifies limits of sparsity-seeking online priming and ties them to concrete interpolation pathologies also observed in LM activations, informing robust feature selection and security-relevant guardrails.
stories_overflow.reason: JEPA/world-model anti-collapse methods and contrastive inverse dynamics propose pretraining objectives relevant to time-series/world-model representation learning, offering alternatives to Gaussian regularizers though not directly TS forecasting.

stories_overflow.title: Task-Conditioned Least-Privilege Learning for Executable Terminal and MCP Agents
stories_overflow.summary: The paper introduces a post-training framework to teach a 4B LLM to select task-conditioned authority in executable terminal and MCP settings, complementing permission gates and sandboxing. It uses deterministic verifiers auditing actions pre- and post-execution along six risk dimensions, combined with task-specific sufficient-authority envelopes to compute excess-privilege signals for optimization, and is trained on Qwen3.5-4B over 1,500 tasks. On 500 held-out tasks (2,896 episodes) the trained model achieves 98.48% safe success vs. 64.36% for the base policy and reduces excess-authority errors from 4.56% to 0.79%, with external tests showing capability retention/prompt-directed improvement and a 400-task continuation indicating generalization with a 6.99 pp reduction in excess-authority events.
stories_overflow.why_it_matters: It proposes and empirically validates a least-privilege post-training signal for tool-use agents, directly addressing excess-authority risks in executable/MCP settings without degrading capabilities.
stories_overflow.reason: Two-stage distillation of tabular foundation models into lightweight predictors is relevant for efficient deployment of foundation-style models, though focused on tabular rather than time-series.

stories_overflow.title: Cross-Corpus Evaluation of Generalizable Vulnerability Detection in IoT Firmware
stories_overflow.summary: The paper introduces IoTVulBench, a human-verified, contamination-screened benchmark for cross-corpus IoT firmware vulnerability detection, and evaluates five model architectures, two tuning methods, and three curriculum strategies with ensemble, distillation, and robustness analyses. Models trained on IoTVulBench outperform matched single-source datasets (MCC 0.58 vs. 0.44 for PrimeVul and 0.39 for D2A), with staged curriculum learning raising MCC to 0.69 and a diversity-optimized ensemble reaching 0.73, surpassing a static analyzer (0.31) and PrimeVul by large margins while maintaining 86% performance under identifier renaming and showing strong calibration and largely faithful explanations. At a 0.5% FPR, the model missed 21% of vulnerabilities versus 71% for the strongest comparator, indicating domain-matched data and curriculum design—not model scale alone—drive generalization in firmware vulnerability detection.
stories_overflow.why_it_matters: Provides a contamination-screened, human-verified benchmark and concrete training/curriculum/ensemble recipes that substantially improve cross-corpus generalization—useful for LLM security evaluation and for designing data- and curriculum-centric pipelines beyond scaling.
stories_overflow.reason: IoT firmware vulnerability detection benchmark is relevant to broader adversarial robustness and benchmark validity but outside core LLM/security or time‑series focus.

stories_overflow.title: Palmyra x6 Technical Report: An Agentic, Tool-Use Model Post-Trained via Anchored Supervised Fine-Tuning
stories_overflow.summary: Palmyra x6 is an enterprise-focused agentic LLM post-trained from an MoE base using Anchored Supervised Fine-Tuning on 626 verified synthetic tool-use trajectories, run for a single epoch with a low LR and a KL anchor to the frozen base, optimized via a Muon+Adam hybrid. It delivers substantial gains for the Writer Agent and compares favorably on public benchmarks, achieving the top BFCL Core score of 0.785 and the highest six-benchmark mean among its cohort. The model is also competitive or leading in the authors’ bias and safety evaluations relative to comparators.
stories_overflow.why_it_matters: Tight, KL-anchored post-training on compact synthetic tool-use traces yielding SOTA-ish agentic performance is directly relevant to secure tool-use alignment and data-efficient post-training strategies for robust, controllable agents.
stories_overflow.reason: Agentic tool-use fine-tuning recipe and anchored SFT on a MoE base is relevant to agent design and deployment risk, though it's an engineering report rather than security-first research.

stories_overflow.title: Ventor-QTest: Threat-Model-Driven Verification of Vendor-Hosted LLM APIs
stories_overflow.summary: The paper formalizes hosted model routing as a stochastic process and introduces Ventor-QTest, a black-box audit requiring no probability outputs, with two components: repeated-request estimating average fidelity loss (AFL) via a null-bias-corrected within-window coarsened-KL, and long-sequence estimating extreme fidelity loss (EFL) from the empirical upper tail of a reference-centered-surprisal statistic. AFL shows strong linear agreement with a logprob-based coarsened-KL comparator across three logprob-capable routing conditions, and 20-run sequence probes across seven route snapshots reveal route-specific EFL variation. AFL/EFL exhibit little association with GPQA-Diamond accuracy, but pronounced EFL aligns with reduced Terminal-Bench pass rates under task exposure, motivating joint reporting when auditing long-horizon agentic tasks; code is open-sourced at the provided link.
stories_overflow.why_it_matters: Offers a practical, probability-free audit to quantify both average and tail fidelity degradation in vendor-hosted LLM routing, directly relevant to red-teaming and reliability of long-horizon agentic deployments.
stories_overflow.reason: Automated vulnerability detection for AI-generated code touches downstream security risks from LLM outputs, useful but more software-security centric than core LLM attack/defense research.

stories_overflow.title: Temporal Leakage in Financial News NLP: A Multi-Architecture Audit with a Regime-Specific M&A Signal
stories_overflow.summary: The paper audits temporal leakage in financial-news direction prediction across 49,799 articles and 16 model–feature setups (TF-IDF, MiniLM, FinBERT, fine-tuned RoBERTa-large/DeBERTa-v3-large, and Llama-3/Qwen2.5 zero/few-shot and LoRA), finding random splits inflate MCC by 1.1×–6.5×, increasing with capacity and feature richness, and that end-to-end FinBERT fine-tuning further amplifies the gap (size-matched ratio 1.75×). Under near-chronological evaluation, only M&A shows a positive locked-test signal (TF-IDF MCC 0.138 train-only, 0.068 after train∪val refit; 10,000-permutation p < 10^{-3}), which does not transfer to FNSPID 2009–2020 U.S. data, suggesting localization to 2024–2025 European-tilted M&A semantics. Three role labelers indicate acquirer-tagged articles as the signal locus, and the authors argue chronological splits purge stale, predictable components, leaving a small, event-localized, lexically shallow residual and call for mandatory leakage audits in financial NLP benchmarks.
stories_overflow.why_it_matters: It quantifies temporal leakage effects across classic NLP and LLM settings, isolates a regime-specific residual signal, and argues for leakage audits—directly informing robust evaluation protocols for security-relevant LLMs and time-series-oriented foundation models.
stories_overflow.reason: ICD forecasting and composing foundation models for longitudinal EHR is relevant to time-series foundation models and prospective forecasting, though clinical focus and integration with search reduces immediate relevance to core TSFM methodology.

stories_overflow.title: No Gaussian Required: Contrastive Inverse Dynamics for JEPA World Models
stories_overflow.summary: The paper proposes Action-Contrastive Masked Transition Modeling (AC-MTM) for JEPA world models, replacing LeWM’s SIGReg Gaussian latent regularizer with a training-only inverse-dynamics head optimized via Action-NCE to prevent representation collapse. This contrastive inverse branch ensures each latent transition identifies its generating action among batch negatives, is discarded after training, and leaves test-time behavior identical to LeWM. AC-MTM matches SIGReg on four standard pixel-control tasks under a matched planner and substantially outperforms it on OGBench Visual Scene (80.0±2.0% vs 58.0±2.0%), suggesting prescribed latent geometry can bottleneck performance; code is released at the provided GitHub link.
stories_overflow.why_it_matters: It offers a distribution-free, target-network-free anti-collapse mechanism for JEPA-style world models that scales to harder visual control, directly relevant to secure, robust representation learning without prescriptive latent priors.
stories_overflow.reason: JEPA world-model work on contrastive inverse dynamics may inform representation objectives useful for time-series or sequential modeling, but it's primarily a world-model / vision-style contribution rather than TSFM security.

stories_overflow.title: Pre-Compiled Pipeline Shards for Distributed LLM Inference on Intel AI PC Fleets
stories_overflow.summary: The work demonstrates pipeline-parallel LLM inference across Intel AI PCs by pre-compiling per-layer shards into OpenVINO graphs, with each node running a shard and passing activations onward. They recover monolithic performance by inserting a beam_idx Gather to trigger OpenVINO’s IndirectKVCache fusion, and further improve throughput via speculative decoding and interleaved multi-user micro-batching. Results: a two-node Llama 3.1 8B INT4 pipeline achieves 1.79x the single-user throughput of the unsplit model for two concurrent users and scales to a four-node deployment serving a 70B model with token-identical outputs to non-speculative decoding; code and scripts are provided.
stories_overflow.why_it_matters: Offers a practical, reproducible recipe to turn idle consumer AI PCs into a distributed LLM serving pool using pipeline sharding with OpenVINO, including concrete tricks (fusion trigger, speculative decoding, interleaved caching) and measured gains.
stories_overflow.reason: Distributed pipeline-parallel inference across Intel AI PCs is relevant to efficient serving and edge deployment for LLMs (useful for cheap red-teaming at scale), but not security or TSFM research.

llm-security.description: Attacks, defenses, and evaluation of LLM systems: jailbreaks, prompt injection, data extraction, red-teaming, alignment-adjacent safety failures with a security framing.

items.title: BASIS: Breach-Aware Selective Prompt Injection Shielding with Prefill Attention Probes
items.summary: The paper addresses over-refusal in prompt-injection defenses by noting that aligned models with robust instructions can withstand many injections, so blanket detection-and-refuse strategies are suboptimal. It proposes BASIS, which uses Attention Competition Ratio features to train two sparse linear probes—an existence probe and a breach probe—that operate in a cascaded, no-extra-inference gating pipeline to detect injections, predict per-sample breaches, and assess instruction robustness. Experiments on four tasks and six open-source LLMs report near-perfect injection detection with substantially reduced over-refusal on safe attack samples, particularly when using robust instruction templates.
items.why_it_matters: It introduces a lightweight, prefill-attention–based, per-sample breach predictor that can cut false refusals without extra LLM calls, complementing existing prompt-injection defenses and aligning with selective prediction ideas familiar from LLM safety and reliability.
items.reason: Persistent semantic entities expose long-lived, cross-boundary contamination in tool-augmented agents — directly relevant to agentic attack surfaces, memory poisoning, and debugging for security.

items.title: Securing AI-Generated Code: A Just-in-Time Vulnerability Detection and Remediation Pipeline
items.summary: The paper introduces an automated just-in-time security pipeline that generates Python from LLMSecEval prompts, detects vulnerabilities with CodeQL, Bandit, and an independent Code Validator LLM, enriches findings with ATT&CK, CWE examples, and best practices, then proposes fixes and re-verifies. Two configurations are compared: P1 uses only enriched validator findings, while P2 also feeds in CodeQL/Bandit outputs; across 80 runs on 26 prompts and four Claude models, P1 reduced static analyzer findings by 9–54% and P2 by 29–69%, with P2 consistently outperforming P1 and showing ~81% modal verdict agreement. Remediation introduced new vulnerabilities in 15–22% of cases (mostly single findings), P2 reduced churn for three models, and pipeline effectiveness did not align with the best code-generation model, as Sonnet 4.6 achieved the lowest residual findings and highest pass rate after P2.
items.why_it_matters: It provides a concrete, empirically tested JIT security loop for LLM-generated code that integrates static analysis, LLM validation, and threat-grounded enrichment—useful for red-teaming LLMs, designing safer codegen pipelines, and benchmarking model–tool orchestration effects.
items.reason: Memory forgery attacks (FARMA) and the Proof-of-Execution defense directly address agent memory manipulation, a high-priority LLM security threat for agentic systems.

items.title: Agent Against Agent: An Agentic System for Automatic Prompt Injection Red Teaming
items.summary: The paper proposes PIMiner, an agentic red-teaming system for prompt injection that trains over sequences of (dataset, target model) pairs to build a strategy library from scratch. At test time, it transfers this library to unseen target LLMs without additional training and uses only a small number of target-agent queries per sample (e.g., 10). Experiments show strong ASR on IPIArena (76.2% Gemini-2.5-Pro, 61.9% GPT-5.1, 42.9% Claude-Sonnet-4.5) and AgentDojo (86.7% Gemini-2.5-Pro, 53.3% GPT-5.1, 40.0% Claude-Sonnet-4.5), outperforming RL-based approaches that generalize poorly.
items.why_it_matters: Offers a transferable, query-efficient prompt-injection attacker that challenges current RL-based red teaming and provides high-quality adversarial data for evaluating and training agent defenses.
items.reason: Automated agentic prompt-injection red teaming addresses prompt-injection attacks and scalable red-team data collection — directly targets core LLM security interests and practical evaluation.

items.title: Do All LLMs Know When They're Being Harmful? A Reproducibility Study of Latent-Space Safety Probes Across Model Families
items.summary: This study reproduces Khatri et al.’s pipeline for training lightweight MLP probes on final-layer activations to detect harmful prompts, matching the original LLaMA-3.1-8B results within 0.37 F1 points (0.2 on BeaverTails). It extends the evaluation across Gemma-4-E4B, Mistral-7B-v0.3, and Qwen2-7B on WildJailbreak, BeaverTails, and AEGIS 2.0, finding F1 within about one point of the LLaMA-3.1-8B values using the same probe architecture. It also assesses nondeterminism by varying seeds and reports that final token latent vectors were invariant to seed across architectures.
items.why_it_matters: Suggests simple latent-space probes generalize across model families with stable activations, informing scalable, low-overhead safety detection for LLMs and complementing guardrail strategies.
items.reason: Reproducibility of latent safety probes across model families evaluates a lightweight detection approach that could scale as a defense or monitoring tool for harmful prompt detection.

Two configurations are compared: P1 uses only enriched validator findings, while P2 also feeds in CodeQL/Bandit outputs; across 80 runs on 26 prompts and four Claude models, P1 reduced static analyzer findings by 9–54% and P2 by 29–69%, with P2 consistently outperforming P1 and showing ~81% modal verdict agreement. Remediation introduced new vulnerabilities in 15–22% of cases (mostly single findings), P2 reduced churn for three models, and pipeline effectiveness did not align with the best code-generation model, as Sonnet 4.6 achieved the lowest residual findings and highest pass rate after P2.
items.why_it_matters: It provides a concrete, empirically tested JIT security loop for LLM-generated code that integrates static analysis, LLM validation, and threat-grounded enrichment—useful for red-teaming LLMs, designing safer codegen pipelines, and benchmarking model–tool orchestration effects.

items.title: Toward Metacognitive One-Shot Indirect Prompt Injection: Strategy Abstraction Via Outcome-Conditioned Reflection
items.summary: The paper introduces SAVOR, a one-shot IPI attack framework that moves adaptation offline via outcome-conditioned reflection over successful and failed trajectories from disjoint training environments, consolidating validated, context-conditioned strategies into a reusable strategy memory. At test time, the frozen memory generates a single payload per unseen target without iterative interaction or feedback, achieving the highest average attack success rate across two benchmarks and three victim models. On Agent Security Bench and the new executable OpenClaw-IPI, SAVOR outperforms the strongest prior attack by 2.5–11.8 points and beats the same injection channel without strategy learning by 23.1 and 28.6 points respectively, with learned memory transferring across defenses.
items.why_it_matters: Demonstrates practical one-shot IPI via offline strategy distillation that generalizes across tools, goals, and defenses—relevant for red-teaming LLM agents and for designing defenses that hold under realistic single-interaction constraints.
items.reason: One-shot indirect prompt injection (IPI) attacks on tool-using agents via offline strategy distillation directly targets agentic attack surfaces and realistic attacker models—highly relevant to LLM security and red-teaming methodology.

items.title: ElasticBack: Stealthy Conditional Backdoor in LLM-Agent Skills via Coupled Trigger-Rule Optimization
items.summary: The paper introduces ElasticBack, a conditional single-skill backdoor for LLM agents that couples a malicious rule R in the skill document with a benign-looking trigger T in user queries, activating only when both appear. It constructs R via semantic-anchored rule injection and then fixes R while evolving T using a stealth-constrained genetic search to optimize attack effectiveness and stealth without modifying model weights. Experiments over three target behaviors (50 skills each) and four agent LLMs show high ASR with near-zero FPR, preserved clean accuracy, cross-model transfer, and evasion of deployment-time defenses, motivating stronger supply-chain defenses for skills.
items.why_it_matters: Highlights a practical, weight-free, conditional backdoor vector in the emerging agent skill ecosystem, relevant to securing tool-using LLMs and evaluating defenses against stealthy trigger-rule couplings.
items.reason: Presents a stealthy conditional backdoor attack targeting agent skills (supply-chain threat) with low-cost single-skill triggers—highly relevant to LLM agent security, tool/skill poisoning, and defense evaluation.

items.title: Evaluating Agentic Learning Harness Capabilities Without Labels via the Scaling Hypothesis
items.summary: The paper proposes an unlabeled evaluation framework for agentic continual learning harnesses, leveraging the scaling hypothesis by using a stronger teacher to provide sparse corrections to a smaller student. Harness quality is scored by the student’s convergence toward the teacher, and across security tasks, model families, and harness designs, teacher-relative lift correlates with improvement against a held-out gold standard. They also find LLM-as-a-judge between similarly powered models provides no usable signal and suggest the same harness can improve a teacher-sized model when humans provide sparse, high-precision corrections.

items.title: LiveHouse-TS: An Open-world Living Benchmark for Time Series Foundation Models
items.summary: The paper introduces LiveHouse-TS, an open-world, living benchmark infrastructure for evaluating TSFMs via prequential testing on real future data rather than static windows. It shifts evaluation focus from snapshot accuracy to continuous temporal validity in environments with seasonality, distribution shifts, and unexpected events, aiming to answer long-term questions about ranking stability and robustness. Streaming evaluations across 11 domains and 17 datasets show that model rankings from static benchmarks dramatically reshuffle under the live protocol.
items.why_it_matters: If you work on LLM security or TSFMs, this exposes how static benchmarks can mislead robustness assessments under shifts, offering an infrastructure to stress-test models’ long-term validity—analogous to live red-teaming and continual evals in LLMs.
items.reason: Directly targets time-series foundation models with a new open-world benchmark capturing distribution shift and continual evaluation — highly relevant to zero-shot/few-shot forecasting, long-horizon robustness, and realistic evaluation methodology.

items.title: CLaST: Context-aware Contrastive VAE for Probabilistic Time Series Forecasting
items.summary: The paper proposes CLaST, a contrastive VAE for probabilistic multivariate time series forecasting that learns context-preserving embeddings via a contrastive loss. It targets the limitation of deep generative forecasters that fail to capture internal temporal dependencies, leading to weak latent representations. Across nine benchmarks, CLaST outperforms strong baselines with up to 16.4% CRPS and 14.4% NMAE gains on short-term tasks, and up to 48.6% CRPS and 25.1% NMAE gains on long-term tasks.

items.title: Personalized Federated Sparse Adaptation of Time-Series Foundation Models
items.summary: The paper proposes a personalized federated sparse adaptation framework for TSFMs in building energy forecasting, using a heterogeneous temporal MoE adapter placed after the pretrained representation and a sequence-level router that assigns each 168-hour window to top-k experts specialized for distinct temporal structures. It evaluates global FL, local training, and personalized FL variants with globally shared vs client-private expert banks across 50 buildings and three TSFM backbones. Results show personalization consistently outperforms Global FL-MoE and Local MoE, the best sparse-adaptation strategy depends on backbone and metric, and routing reveals client-level expert specialization, expert concentration, and near-uniform routing across backbones, implying adaptation should be client- and backbone-aware.

items.title: Do All LLMs Know When They're Being Harmful? A Reproducibility Study of Latent-Space Safety Probes Across Model Families
items.summary: This study reproduces Khatri et al.’s pipeline for training lightweight MLP probes on final-layer activations to detect harmful prompts, matching the original LLaMA-3.1-8B results within 0.37 F1 points (0.2 on BeaverTails). It extends the evaluation across Gemma-4-E4B, Mistral-7B-v0.3, and Qwen2-7B on WildJailbreak, BeaverTails, and AEGIS 2.0, finding F1 within about one point of the LLaMA-3.1-8B values using the same probe architecture. It also assesses nondeterminism by varying seeds and reports that final token latent vectors were invariant to seed across architectures.
items.why_it_matters: Suggests simple latent-space probes generalize across model families with stable activations, informing scalable, low-overhead safety detection for LLMs and complementing guardrail strategies.

items.title: Align-RAG: Alignment Is All You Need for TSFM In-Context Learning
items.summary: The paper introduces Align-RAG, a training-free method that applies closed-form amplitude rescaling and integer-lag phase alignment to retrieved past–future windows before feeding them to a frozen TSFM. On a frozen Chronos-Bolt, it outperforms a state-of-the-art trained retrieval adapter across seven benchmark datasets (average −3.75% MSE), and it also improves zero-shot MSE by 2.5%–13.7% on four additional frozen TSFMs without per-backbone tuning. Analysis shows aligned demonstrations induce prediction shifts in frozen backbones that track a closed-form ridge predictor on the same pairs, with a future-shuffle control ruling out futures-averaging, suggesting frozen TSFMs already support dynamic in-context use of retrievals.
items.why_it_matters: It challenges the need for learned fusion in RAG for forecasting by showing closed-form alignment on frozen backbones yields SOTA gains and ridge-like in-context adaptation, a strong baseline relevant to LLM alignment and retrieval studies.
items.reason: DASH improves on-policy self-distillation for reasoning models with temporally-adaptive supervision horizons — relevant to improving RL-style fine-tuning and evaluation of reasoning/judging behavior and scalable red-teaming.

items.title: ProbGuard: Calibrated Safety Risk Estimation from LLM Output Distributions
items.summary: ProbGuard reframes LLM safety assessment as probabilistic risk estimation over the model’s early output distribution rather than deterministic classification on completed token sequences. It estimates the probability of unsafe continuation via Monte Carlo over generated prefix distributions and calibrates this risk through post-training, enabling early stopping of unsafe generations. Empirically, it achieves the best calibration across nine model–dataset settings (average Brier and ECE reduced by 79.6% and 71.9% vs. the best baseline) and caps jailbreak attack success to ≤1% after only the first ten decoding steps.
items.why_it_matters: It operationalizes distribution-aware, early-stage safety control with strong calibration—useful for red-teaming defenses, risk-sensitive deployment, and aligning with probabilistic guardrail research and time-series-style forecasting over generation trajectories.
items.reason: Proposes a novel metric (feature nonlocality) to assess abstraction level of learned features from sparse autoencoders; useful for mechanistic interpretability and evaluating claims about high-level features relevant to jailbreak/mechanistic work.

items.title: BASIS: Breach-Aware Selective Prompt Injection Shielding with Prefill Attention Probes
items.summary: The paper addresses over-refusal in prompt-injection defenses by noting that aligned models with robust instructions can withstand many injections, so blanket detection-and-refuse strategies are suboptimal. It proposes BASIS, which uses Attention Competition Ratio features to train two sparse linear probes—an existence probe and a breach probe—that operate in a cascaded, no-extra-inference gating pipeline to detect injections, predict per-sample breaches, and assess instruction robustness. Experiments on four tasks and six open-source LLMs report near-perfect injection detection with substantially reduced over-refusal on safe attack samples, particularly when using robust instruction templates.
items.why_it_matters: It introduces a lightweight, prefill-attention–based, per-sample breach predictor that can cut false refusals without extra LLM calls, complementing existing prompt-injection defenses and aligning with selective prediction ideas familiar from LLM safety and reliability.

items.title: The Horizon Gap: Planning, Memory, Execution, Training, and Evaluation for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
items.summary: The paper defines the horizon gap: LLMs that excel in single-pass reasoning still fail on multi-hour, multi-step tasks, and surveys 1,547 arXiv papers (2024–2026) collected via a systematic seed harvest with a 26.8% bleed filter plus targeted supplementation. A recurring finding is that outcome-only signals become uninformative as horizons increase, prompting methods that create denser step-level signals (e.g., process rewards, credit assignment, trajectory diagnostics), and the paper highlights open measurement problems around decomposing model vs. harness capability, correlated bias in process-level signals, and the possibility of a general predictive theory of long-horizon reliability.

items.title: Deployable Per-Instance Multi-Layer Activation Steering for Large Language Models
items.summary: The paper shows that in activation steering, the optimal injection layers vary per input, with per-instance multi-layer selection outperforming any fixed global layer set across six binary persona traits on two 8B models. A greedy layer-ranking rule based on single-layer marginal effects nearly matches a per-instance oracle but requires gold labels, so the authors train a prompt-only predictor to mimic it and propose a deployable recipe: a prompt-based per-instance layer ranker, a classifier to infer steering direction, and an adaptive gate that limits layers by short steered passes. This deployable approach recovers most of the oracle’s gains, avoids dropping below unsteered baselines on average, reduces fluency collapse relative to strong global selection, and is supported by a mechanistic account emphasizing direction over magnitude that explains misdirection flips, collapse from over-steering, and unsteerable ceilings.
items.why_it_matters: It operationalizes per-instance, label-free activation steering with adaptive multi-layer control, offering a practical path to safer, targeted behavior edits without sacrificing fluency—relevant to red-teaming defenses and controllable generation, and conceptually aligned with direction-based causal hypotheses familiar in interpretability.

items.title: DSPrompt: Dynamic Soft Prompt Defense Against M-RAG Corruption
items.summary: DSPrompt defends M-RAG by inserting a few learnable soft prompts into each layer of frozen visual/text encoders, using a shallow-to-deep length schedule to reshape embedding semantics without altering the retrieval pipeline. It trains these prompts via a dynamic min-max scheme with an online multimodal attacker that crafts hard adversarial documents, while the defender pushes them out of top-k and preserves benign ranking/diversity; the defended encoder can be precomputed and indexed like standard dense retrieval with <1% extra parameters and no per-query overhead. Experiments on four benchmarks and three poisoning attacks show substantial reductions in attack success and poison retrieval rates with near-lossless retrieval utility and generation fidelity, outperforming baselines at lower computational cost.
items.why_it_matters: Offers a low-overhead, precomputable defense that hardens retrievers against embedding-space poisoning without query-time detectors—relevant for securing M-RAG and retrieval backbones in LLM pipelines.

items.title: HarnessSafe: Evaluating Safety Across Persistent Carriers in Agent Harnesses
items.summary: The paper introduces HarnessSafe, a benchmark of 328 executable cases spanning seven persistent-carrier families to assess delayed safety risks in agent harnesses that persist state across tasks and sessions. Each case is defined as a Persistent-Risk Lifecycle that traces attacker influence from entry through cross-carrier persistence to a benign trigger and an observable violation, and a multi-stage, trace-based evaluation measures how far each attack progresses and where it is stopped. Experiments indicate containment is carrier-specific and depends strongly on the harness-model configuration, with both harness and model shaping outcomes and attack success rates failing to capture lifecycle progression patterns.
items.why_it_matters: It offers a carrier-aware, trace-based methodology and dataset to dissect how safety risks propagate across memory/tools/skills in agentic systems—complementing coarse success-rate metrics and informing defense design in LLM agents and persistent pipelines.

items.title: Security Assessment of DeepSeek Harness with A.I.G: Evaluating Resistance to Indirect Prompt Injection
items.summary: This work evaluates indirect prompt injection against DeepSeek Harness using AI-Infra-Guard to generate tests, deliver controlled taint across 16 channels and two carrier modes, run 14,560 executions, and analyze traces with both rule-based and LLM-based judges. The strongest observed attack success rates are 17.0% under LLMJudge for a fake-completion attack (text), 25.5% under RuleJudge for hidden Unicode (file), and 16.0% under RuleJudge for the skills channel (file), with LLMJudge assigning more partial compliance than RuleJudge (7.3% vs. 2.0%). The study connects outcomes to DSH’s handling of tool results, extra contexts, and tool-call policy hooks, and proposes controls between untrusted content and sensitive actions, with code released at the linked repository.
items.why_it_matters: Provides a large-scale, reproducible, channel- and payload-stratified benchmark of indirect prompt injection on an agentic LLM stack with dual judges, informing defense design and evaluation baselines.

items.title: Measure, Don't Optimize: Forecasting Recovery in LLM Unlearning
items.summary: The paper introduces J-Access, an inference-time audit that projects intermediate representations into vocabulary space to measure how often target concepts remain accessible along the output pathway, hypothesizing that residual accessibility predicts recovery susceptibility. Auditing 398 public unlearned models across eight methods, they find most retain accessibility above a retain-only gold level, pre-attack accessibility predicts recovery speed and extent at the model level (but not per-fact), and directly minimizing J-Access causes the model to hide knowledge from the audit while increasing post-attack recovery. They conclude J-Access is useful as a model-level diagnostic for residual susceptibility and caution against turning internal audits into optimization targets without validation.
items.why_it_matters: Offers an actionable, model-level risk signal for unlearning robustness and a clear warning about Goodharting internal audits—relevant for designing secure unlearning and audit pipelines in LLMs.

items.title: Task-Conditioned Least-Privilege Learning for Executable Terminal and MCP Agents
items.summary: The paper introduces a post-training framework to teach a 4B LLM to select task-conditioned authority in executable terminal and MCP settings, complementing permission gates and sandboxing. It uses deterministic verifiers auditing actions pre- and post-execution along six risk dimensions, combined with task-specific sufficient-authority envelopes to compute excess-privilege signals for optimization, and is trained on Qwen3.5-4B over 1,500 tasks. On 500 held-out tasks (2,896 episodes) the trained model achieves 98.48% safe success vs. 64.36% for the base policy and reduces excess-authority errors from 4.56% to 0.79%, with external tests showing capability retention/prompt-directed improvement and a 400-task continuation indicating generalization with a 6.99 pp reduction in excess-authority events.
items.why_it_matters: It proposes and empirically validates a least-privilege post-training signal for tool-use agents, directly addressing excess-authority risks in executable/MCP settings without degrading capabilities.

items.title: Palmyra x6 Technical Report: An Agentic, Tool-Use Model Post-Trained via Anchored Supervised Fine-Tuning
items.summary: Palmyra x6 is an enterprise-focused agentic LLM post-trained from an MoE base using Anchored Supervised Fine-Tuning on 626 verified synthetic tool-use trajectories, run for a single epoch with a low LR and a KL anchor to the frozen base, optimized via a Muon+Adam hybrid. It delivers substantial gains for the Writer Agent and compares favorably on public benchmarks, achieving the top BFCL Core score of 0.785 and the highest six-benchmark mean among its cohort. The model is also competitive or leading in the authors’ bias and safety evaluations relative to comparators.

items.title: A Four-Axis Trustworthiness Benchmark for LLM-as-Judge in Principle-Based Regulation
items.summary: The paper argues LLM-as-judge for principle-based regulation must be evaluated on four axes: accuracy, paraphrase robustness, adversarial robustness, and calibration, and releases Principle-Bench with 168 FCA-aligned crypto promotion scenarios including paraphrase, keyword-stuffing, and boundary perturbations. It introduces Ceca, a calibrated, auditable assessor emitting per-exemplar counterfactual attributions, and evaluates keyword counting, three sentence-transformer embedders, an open-weight LLM-judge, and a calibrated cascade. Results show no method dominates all axes; a strong 120B judge drops from 0.74 to 0.27 accuracy under keyword-stuffed Consumer Duty inputs and another family’s judge agrees at κ=0.16 on that split, underscoring model-specific failures and the need for per-principle adversarial deception reporting and post-hoc calibration alongside aggregate accuracy.

It distinguishes long-horizon, long-context, and long-term memory, and organizes the literature into six lifecycle categories (planning, memory, execution, training, evaluation, foundations/safety) crossed with where horizons are carried (within-context, within-task-beyond-context, cross-task-persistent). A recurring finding is that outcome-only signals become uninformative as horizons increase, prompting methods that create denser step-level signals (e.g., process rewards, credit assignment, trajectory diagnostics), and the paper highlights open measurement problems around decomposing model vs. harness capability, correlated bias in process-level signals, and the possibility of a general predictive theory of long-horizon reliability.
items.why_it_matters: It maps the long-horizon agent landscape, clarifies signal-design pitfalls, and surfaces open measurement issues directly relevant to LLM safety, agent reliability, and long-horizon training/eval design.
items.reason: Directly targets long-horizon failure modes in LLM agents—survey synthesizes planning, memory, evaluation and training gaps relevant to agentic security and long-context modeling.

items.title: From Runnable to Verifiable: An Independent Reproducibility Study of LLM/Agent-Driven Vulnerability Validation Artifacts
items.summary: This pre-registered reproducibility audit examines LLM/agent-driven vulnerability validation artifacts across 104 papers (2023–2026), finding only 59 with publicly reachable artifacts and executing 18 paper-level workflows and 102 anchor benchmark cases. It reports high mismatch and fragility: 58/102 anchor cases have internal CVE IDs diverging from directory labels; only 10/18 artifacts run end-to-end at R0 (11/18 after R1 env-only fixes); and embedded oracles are unreliable, with 20/30 patched-counterfactuals still signaling and 7/19 negative controls triggering, yielding oracle sensitivity 60% and specificity 45%. The study argues that vulnerable-build triggers are not CVE-specific evidence without a clean patched counterfactual and offers a reusable, pre-registered protocol (post-conditions, R0/R1 repair ladder, G1–G3 evidence levels, patched-counterfactual oracles) for the community.
items.why_it_matters: It surfaces concrete failure modes and a reusable protocol for verifying LLM/agent security claims—directly informing eval design, oracle construction, and counterfactual controls for both LLM security and time-series-style benchmark reproducibility.
items.reason: ActBench proposes an execution-trajectory-based behavioral safety benchmark for cowork agents, directly applicable to evaluating agent risks like data leakage and unauthorized actions—highly relevant for tooling and red-teaming.

items.title: Intern-S2-Preview: Scientific Agentic Foundation Model
items.summary: Intern-S2-Preview introduces scientific agentic foundation models trained via multimodal pretraining on rendered scientific documents, interleaved image-text, and diverse scientific corpora, followed by a unified post-training stack of SFT, scalable multi-task RL, black- and white-box agentic RL, and on-policy distillation. The pipeline adds practical rollout/training techniques—partial rollout with off-policy correction, adaptive length regularization, online speculative decoding, robust multi-task optimization, and trace-aware experience assembly—and explores architecture-level extensions: a 397B model with time series modules for efficient long-sequence understanding and numerical forecasting, plus a separate Memory Decoder path for rapid specialization without changing the frozen backbone. Evaluations report competitive or leading results across scientific, multimodal, agentic, and general-purpose benchmarks, with time-series gains on SciTS and a MemDec-4B extension improving Biology-Instructions average from 56.92 to 60.32 without modifying the 397B backbone.
items.why_it_matters: Brings a concrete agentic RL + multimodal + TS forecasting stack with stability tricks and a memory-augmented specialization path relevant to secure tool-use agents and time-series LLMs.
items.reason: Agentic multimodal scientific foundation model work intersects with agentic-system attack surfaces and long-horizon reasoning, relevant for security analysis though not focused on adversarial robustness.

items.title: Can a Lightweight Multimodal Model Estimate LLM Reasoning Performance? A Study for Compute-Optimal Document Inference
items.summary: The paper introduces BudgetDoc, a multimodal benchmark with explicit supervision for model-budget-performance trade-offs on three document tasks, addressing the cost and over-thinking issues of uniform inference budgets in LLMs. Using BudgetDoc, the authors train DRB, a ~1B-parameter pre-flight estimator (SigLIP-2 + Qwen3-0.6B) that predicts ordinal model performance across budget levels with a weighted F1 of 0.753. DRB enables dynamic reasoning budget allocation across five frontier models and three datasets, matching or improving F1 over always-maximum-budget baselines in 9/15 settings while reducing cost, and shows preliminary promise for cross-model selection generalization.
items.why_it_matters: It offers a practical path to compute-optimal, layout-aware reasoning allocation and model selection for document tasks, directly relevant to secure and efficient deployment of reasoning LLMs.
items.reason: A lightweight multimodal estimator to predict LLM reasoning performance (compute-budget tradeoffs) is useful for compute-optimal allocation and efficient red-teaming at scale, relevant to security/serving tradeoffs.

items.title: Security Assessment of DeepSeek Harness with A.I.G: Evaluating Resistance to Indirect Prompt Injection
items.summary: This work evaluates indirect prompt injection against DeepSeek Harness using AI-Infra-Guard to generate tests, deliver controlled taint across 16 channels and two carrier modes, run 14,560 executions, and analyze traces with both rule-based and LLM-based judges. The strongest observed attack success rates are 17.0% under LLMJudge for a fake-completion attack (text), 25.5% under RuleJudge for hidden Unicode (file), and 16.0% under RuleJudge for the skills channel (file), with LLMJudge assigning more partial compliance than RuleJudge (7.3% vs. 2.0%). The study connects outcomes to DSH’s handling of tool results, extra contexts, and tool-call policy hooks, and proposes controls between untrusted content and sensitive actions, with code released at the linked repository.
items.why_it_matters: Provides a large-scale, reproducible, channel- and payload-stratified benchmark of indirect prompt injection on an agentic LLM stack with dual judges, informing defense design and evaluation baselines.
items.reason: Black-box auditing of vendor-hosted LLM APIs via statistical repeated-query testing is highly relevant for red-teaming, API threat models, and evaluation methodology.

items.title: Towards a Risk Assessment of Malicious Skill Files in Coding Agents
items.summary: The paper studies the attack surface introduced by agent skill folders in autonomous coding agents and presents an adversarial skill-synthesis method that converts 471 real shell commands into 2,826 benign-looking skills mapped to 11 ATT&CK tactics using six LLMs. It introduces a reproducible evaluation pipeline with stratification, evidence anchoring, refusal veto, and a deterministic declared-intent override, using a three-judge LLM panel validated against a blind human gold standard (κ=0.85). items.title: Align-RAG: Alignment Is All You Need for TSFM In-Context Learning
items.summary: The paper introduces Align-RAG, a training-free method that applies closed-form amplitude rescaling and integer-lag phase alignment to retrieved past–future windows before feeding them to a frozen TSFM. On a frozen Chronos-Bolt, it outperforms a state-of-the-art trained retrieval adapter across seven benchmark datasets (average −3.75% MSE), and it also improves zero-shot MSE by 2.5%–13.7% on four additional frozen TSFMs without per-backbone tuning. Analysis shows aligned demonstrations induce prediction shifts in frozen backbones that track a closed-form ridge predictor on the same pairs, with a future-shuffle control ruling out futures-averaging, suggesting frozen TSFMs already support dynamic in-context use of retrievals.
items.why_it_matters: It challenges the need for learned fusion in RAG for forecasting by showing closed-form alignment on frozen backbones yields SOTA gains and ridge-like in-context adaptation, a strong baseline relevant to LLM alignment and retrieval studies.
items.reason: DASH improves on-policy self-distillation for reasoning models with temporally-adaptive supervision horizons — relevant to improving RL-style fine-tuning and evaluation of reasoning/judging behavior and scalable red-teaming.

items.title: Ventor-QTest: Threat-Model-Driven Verification of Vendor-Hosted LLM APIs
items.summary: The paper formalizes hosted model routing as a stochastic process and introduces Ventor-QTest, a black-box audit requiring no probability outputs, with two components: repeated-request estimating average fidelity loss (AFL) via a null-bias-corrected within-window coarsened-KL, and long-sequence estimating extreme fidelity loss (EFL) from the empirical upper tail of a reference-centered-surprisal statistic. AFL shows strong linear agreement with a logprob-based coarsened-KL comparator across three logprob-capable routing conditions, and 20-run sequence probes across seven route snapshots reveal route-specific EFL variation. AFL/EFL exhibit little association with GPQA-Diamond accuracy, but pronounced EFL aligns with reduced Terminal-Bench pass rates under task exposure, motivating joint reporting when auditing long-horizon agentic tasks; code is open-sourced at the provided link.
items.why_it_matters: Offers a practical, probability-free audit to quantify both average and tail fidelity degradation in vendor-hosted LLM routing, directly relevant to red-teaming and reliability of long-horizon agentic deployments.
items.reason: Automated vulnerability detection for AI-generated code touches downstream security risks from LLM outputs, useful but more software-security centric than core LLM attack/defense research.

items.title: No Gaussian Required: Contrastive Inverse Dynamics for JEPA World Models
items.summary: The paper proposes Action-Contrastive Masked Transition Modeling (AC-MTM) for JEPA world models, replacing LeWM’s SIGReg Gaussian latent regularizer with a training-only inverse-dynamics head optimized via Action-NCE to prevent representation collapse. This contrastive inverse branch ensures each latent transition identifies its generating action among batch negatives, is discarded after training, and leaves test-time behavior identical to LeWM. AC-MTM matches SIGReg on four standard pixel-control tasks under a matched planner and substantially outperforms it on OGBench Visual Scene (80.0±2.0% vs 58.0±2.0%), suggesting prescribed latent geometry can bottleneck performance; code is released at the provided GitHub link.
items.why_it_matters: It offers a distribution-free, target-network-free anti-collapse mechanism for JEPA-style world models that scales to harder visual control, directly relevant to secure, robust representation learning without prescriptive latent priors.
items.reason: JEPA world-model work on contrastive inverse dynamics may inform representation objectives useful for time-series or sequential modeling, but it's primarily a world-model / vision-style contribution rather than TSFM security.

llm-security.title: HarnessSafe: Evaluating Safety Across Persistent Carriers in Agent Harnesses
llm-security.summary: The paper introduces HarnessSafe, a benchmark of 328 executable cases spanning seven persistent-carrier families to assess delayed safety risks in agent harnesses that persist state across tasks and sessions. Each case is defined as a Persistent-Risk Lifecycle that traces attacker influence from entry through cross-carrier persistence to a benign trigger and an observable violation, and a multi-stage, trace-based evaluation measures how far each attack progresses and where it is stopped. Experiments indicate containment is carrier-specific and depends strongly on the harness-model configuration, with both harness and model shaping outcomes and attack success rates failing to capture lifecycle progression patterns.
llm-security.why_it_matters: It offers a carrier-aware, trace-based methodology and dataset to dissect how safety risks propagate across memory/tools/skills in agentic systems—complementing coarse success-rate metrics and informing defense design in LLM agents and persistent pipelines.
llm-security.reason: Benchmarks delayed safety risks from persistent carriers in agent harnesses; directly targets attack surfaces (memory, tools, skills), evaluation methodology, and end-to-end exploit propagation — highly relevant to LLM security and agentic threat models.

llm-security.title: Toward Metacognitive One-Shot Indirect Prompt Injection: Strategy Abstraction Via Outcome-Conditioned Reflection
llm-security.summary: The paper introduces SAVOR, a one-shot IPI attack framework that moves adaptation offline via outcome-conditioned reflection over successful and failed trajectories from disjoint training environments, consolidating validated, context-conditioned strategies into a reusable strategy memory. At test time, the frozen memory generates a single payload per unseen target without iterative interaction or feedback, achieving the highest average attack success rate across two benchmarks and three victim models. On Agent Security Bench and the new executable OpenClaw-IPI, SAVOR outperforms the strongest prior attack by 2.5–11.8 points and beats the same injection channel without strategy learning by 23.1 and 28.6 points respectively, with learned memory transferring across defenses.
llm-security.why_it_matters: Demonstrates practical one-shot IPI via offline strategy distillation that generalizes across tools, goals, and defenses—relevant for red-teaming LLM agents and for designing defenses that hold under realistic single-interaction constraints.
llm-security.reason: One-shot indirect prompt injection (IPI) attacks on tool-using agents via offline strategy distillation directly targets agentic attack surfaces and realistic attacker models—highly relevant to LLM security and red-teaming methodology.

llm-security.title: ElasticBack: Stealthy Conditional Backdoor in LLM-Agent Skills via Coupled Trigger-Rule Optimization
llm-security.summary: The paper introduces ElasticBack, a conditional single-skill backdoor for LLM agents that couples a malicious rule R in the skill document with a benign-looking trigger T in user queries, activating only when both appear. It constructs R via semantic-anchored rule injection and then fixes R while evolving T using a stealth-constrained genetic search to optimize attack effectiveness and stealth without modifying model weights. Experiments over three target behaviors (50 skills each) and four agent LLMs show high ASR with near-zero FPR, preserved clean accuracy, cross-model transfer, and evasion of deployment-time defenses, motivating stronger supply-chain defenses for skills.
llm-security.why_it_matters: Highlights a practical, weight-free, conditional backdoor vector in the emerging agent skill ecosystem, relevant to securing tool-using LLMs and evaluating defenses against stealthy trigger-rule couplings.
llm-security.reason: Presents a stealthy conditional backdoor attack targeting agent skills (supply-chain threat) with low-cost single-skill triggers—highly relevant to LLM agent security, tool/skill poisoning, and defense evaluation.

llm-security.title: On Understanding, Identifying, and Mitigating Vulnerabilities in Agentic Large Language Models
llm-security.summary: This paper reviews 85 papers (2023–2025) on security of agentic LLMs, selected via a PRISMA 2020 systematic process from 743 records, finding attack work outpaces defenses by 3.9:1. It reports that perception-layer vulnerabilities (prompt injection, jailbreaking, adversarial perturbations) dominate at 66%, while action-layer issues (tool misuse, code injection, sandbox escape) are only 4.7%, with code execution at 3.5% and tool-augmented agents at 12%. The authors propose a four-layer taxonomy (perception, brain, action, interaction) covering 13 vulnerability types, identify seven open problems focused on containment, and argue that weak isolation and architectural coupling let failures propagate across layers.
llm-security.why_it_matters: It quantifies where current security work is misaligned with real agentic risk surfaces and offers a layered taxonomy and containment-focused agenda that can guide rigorous evaluations and defenses for tool-using, code-executing LLM agents.
llm-security.reason: Systematic review focused on vulnerabilities unique to agentic LLMs (tool use, persistent memory, state changes) directly matches the reader's primary interest in agent attack surfaces and red‑teaming.

llm-security.title: Foundation Agents Meet Agentic Deep Research: Evidence-Grounded Clinical Code Forecasting
llm-security.summary: The paper tackles prospective multi-label next-encounter ICD forecasting by composing structured EHR and language foundation models with medical search and ICD dictionaries in a DeepResearch workflow called ICD-Deepresearch. It uses SparseEHR to create an EHR Prior for bounded research expansion, integrates an independent GPT-5 Direct Forecast for complementary candidates, and performs final validation/dedup/ranking with separate rationale generation that doesn’t alter predictions. On MIMIC-III/IV it reports patient-averaged precision/recall of 24.60/35.09% and 25.14/48.32%, and physicians rate its retrieved documents more useful than standalone GPT-5 web search and Medical Deep Research, with improvements over registered local comparators.
llm-security.why_it_matters: Demonstrates an agentic, evidence-grounded composition of EHR and LLM predictors that yields measurable gains in future-code forecasting and retrieval usefulness—relevant to secure, auditable multi-agent workflows for clinical time-series forecasting.

llm-security.title: SCALE: State-Calibrated Latent Embeddings for JEPA Planning in the Right Geometry
llm-security.summary: The paper studies JEPA-style planning where terminal embedding costs depend on representation geometry, comparing DINO-WM’s pretrained space to LeWM’s end-to-end SIGReg embeddings and noting that DINO-WM’s top PCs retain more state information, which interacts with Euclidean costs. It introduces SCALE, a training-time regularizer that aligns sampled latent pairwise distances with standardized task-state distances to induce DINO-like geometric properties in LeWM without replacing its encoder. Across five tasks, three solvers, and five compute budgets, SCALE consistently improves task–solver averages over LeWM, while a latent-to-state regression control achieves similar decodability but not distance alignment and yields less consistent planning gains, adding no planning-time overhead.
llm-security.why_it_matters: Shows that not just decodability but latent geometry (variance structure and distance alignment to state) materially affects JEPA planning quality, offering a lightweight regularizer to tune geometry for better planner performance.

llm-security.title: Enhancing Anomaly Resilience in Research Networks: A Large-Scale Forecasting Benchmark for Dynamic Security Baselining
llm-security.summary: The paper introduces a high-fidelity traffic forecasting framework to create dynamic security baselines for RENs, addressing the challenge that elephant flows resemble volumetric attacks to conventional monitors. Using a 57-day Internet2 dataset (13.7B packets across ten backbone routers), it benchmarks six forecasting model families, including SARIMA and long-sequence architectures (TiDE, PatchTST), over 960 configurations. Results show advanced models—especially TiDE—reduce baseline prediction error by 30–42% (p < 0.001) and that a new anomaly-integration strategy yields a 3.3% robustness gain under noise, improving separation of scientific bursts from anomalies.
llm-security.why_it_matters: It provides a statistically validated, large-scale benchmark showing long-sequence LLM-adjacent forecasters (e.g., TiDE/PatchTST) materially improve dynamic baselining for REN security, informing robust anomaly detection under bursty traffic.
llm-security.reason: AMS detects safety-training modifications via activation geometry across major model families—highly pertinent to model integrity, detection of fine-tune/backdoor changes and LLM security for deployed models.

llm-security.title: When Do PEFT Adaptations Leak Structure? Measuring Black-Box Structural Bounds in Public-Base Model Services
llm-security.summary: The paper introduces VectorHijack-SR, a black-box measurement method that turns paired victim/base residuals into calibrated bounds over PEFT family, layer locality, and coarse rank, using aggregated query-level statistics and a service-disjoint classifier plus a cross-fitted hierarchical rejector to test LoRA-manifold membership. Empirically, family leakage exceeds chance across multiple backbones/tasks, rank inference varies by task, the rejector attains AUROC 0.804 and high known-set accuracy but struggles with structurally close DoRA/LoRA+head, and exact-version linkage on held-out LoRA-r64 services reaches AUC 0.940. Despite measurable structural leakage, experiments show a visibility–exploitability gap: two-stage recovery offers no fair-budget query savings, posterior-selected PEFT underperforms distill-then-convert PEFT, and free-running generation remains near chance.
llm-security.why_it_matters: It provides concrete, black-box evidence and metrics for structural leakage from PEFTed services with known bases, informing red-team audits, model fingerprinting, and security evaluations of adapter deployment choices.
llm-security.reason: Directly studies information leakage from PEFT adapters in public-base services — highly relevant to model extraction, PIi leakage, and red-team measurement for LLM security.

llm-security.title: Deployable Per-Instance Multi-Layer Activation Steering for Large Language Models
llm-security.summary: The paper shows that in activation steering, the optimal injection layers vary per input, with per-instance multi-layer selection outperforming any fixed global layer set across six binary persona traits on two 8B models. A greedy layer-ranking rule based on single-layer marginal effects nearly matches a per-instance oracle but requires gold labels, so the authors train a prompt-only predictor to mimic it and propose a deployable recipe: a prompt-based per-instance layer ranker, a classifier to infer steering direction, and an adaptive gate that limits layers by short steered passes. This deployable approach recovers most of the oracle’s gains, avoids dropping below unsteered baselines on average, reduces fluency collapse relative to strong global selection, and is supported by a mechanistic account emphasizing direction over magnitude that explains misdirection flips, collapse from over-steering, and unsteerable ceilings.
llm-security.why_it_matters: It operationalizes per-instance, label-free activation steering with adaptive multi-layer control, offering a practical path to safer, targeted behavior edits without sacrificing fluency—relevant to red-teaming defenses and controllable generation, and conceptually aligned with direction-based causal hypotheses familiar in interpretability.
llm-security.reason: Per-instance multi-layer activation steering directly targets editing/model control at inference time—relevant to attack/defense surfaces, deployment, and efficient selective interventions for LLM security and agent behavior.

llm-security.title: SkillsMetric: Mapping the Detection Boundary of Static Analysis for Malicious Agent Skills
llm-security.summary: This work introduces SkillsMetric, a five-stage static analysis framework that scores LLM agent skills across pattern density, statistical anomaly, dataflow taint, import anomaly, and capability mismatch. Using an adversarial dataset of 2,266 skills covering 16 attack types and the SkillMD-138K corpus, it reports AUC 0.93 and 5-fold CV F1 73.4%±0.5%, with 93% detection for data exfiltration and steganographic payloads. It also exposes blind spots—0% detection for host destruction via common shell commands and 42% for prompt injection—arguing static analysis alone is insufficient and should be paired with semantic review in defense-in-depth.
llm-security.why_it_matters: Directly maps the detection boundary of static analysis for agent skills, highlighting failure modes (e.g., prompt injection, host destruction) that inform red-teaming, hybrid detection pipelines, and security benchmarks for LLM agents.
llm-security.reason: Static analysis scoring of agent 'skills' maps to supply-chain and capability-based attack surfaces for LLM agents and helps red-teaming/defense of tool-augmented systems.

llm-security.title: An Empirical Study of Output-to-Input Loops for Black-Box Backdoor Detection in Fine-Tuned Open-Weight LLMs
llm-security.summary: The paper proposes self-feeding, a black-box test that recursively feeds a model’s outputs back as inputs to drift toward fine-tuning data, enabling backdoor discovery without training data, clean baselines, or trigger knowledge. Evaluated on six open-weight LLMs (3B–15B) with eleven backdoor categories and twenty prompts over up to ten steps, self-feeding detects backdoors in five models with 92.0% pooled precision, while a same-prompt baseline succeeds on only one of 120 prompt-model pairs; some prompts (jokes, arithmetic, coffee recipes) reach triggers in a few steps. Despite low per-prompt recall (19.2%), multi-prompt use raises model-level detection, though one model never triggers and there are two false positives; truncating to four steps preserves 100% model-level precision and cuts queries by 60%.
llm-security.why_it_matters: Offers a cheap, black-box, text-only stress test that surfaces fine-tune data modes (including backdoors) via output-to-input loops, complementing existing evals for open-weight LLMs and informing detection strategies for security-focused and time-series-style iterative generation analyses.
llm-security.reason: Black‑box self‑feeding method for detecting backdoors in fine‑tuned open LLMs is directly applicable to model vetting, backdoor detection, and practical security checks for deployed models.

llm-security.title: Generating Attacks for LLMs with GFlowNets
llm-security.summary: The work proposes an automated, human-independent red teaming framework that trains an attacker LLM via GFlowNets to probe a specified victim LLM and yield a quantitative robustness score. The approach targets generating more effective English adversarial inputs than existing benchmarks and, uniquely, introduces Turkish-language attack generation.

llm-security.title: Measuring Task-Agnostic Training Data Influence Across Language Model Pretraining
llm-security.summary: The paper introduces a task-agnostic measure of training data influence that quantifies how much an example’s gradient update reduces the squared distance to a run’s final parameters, estimated from intermediate checkpoints without retraining. Applied to 18 Pythia and PolyPythia configurations, the method reveals systematic temporal shifts in influential data: literature-related data align more with the parameter trajectory early, while STEM data align more later. This qualitative crossover is broadly consistent across configurations, offering a tractable trajectory-level perspective that complements task-based influence analyses.
llm-security.why_it_matters: Gives a practical, retraining-free way to map which data sources steer pretraining trajectories over time, informing data curation, curriculum, and security-relevant provenance audits for LLMs.
llm-security.reason: Proposes a task-agnostic measure of individual-example influence during LM pretraining which is highly relevant to data provenance, extraction/attribution, contamination, and training-time attack/defense analysis.

llm-security.title: The More Popular, The Harder to Forget: Adaptive Popularity for LLM Unlearning
llm-security.summary: The paper observes that popular facts are memorized more deeply in LLM pretraining and are harder to unlearn, while prior unlearning methods apply uniform gradient pressure regardless of frequency. It proposes AdaPop, which scales unlearning pressure using local token confidence and a per-fact popularity-dependent exponent from an external proxy, and uses a dual-ascent controller to automatically tune the retain penalty each epoch. On three model families and two benchmarks, AdaPop reduces leakage of forgotten content by ~5x on paraphrases and ~1.6x on adversarial reformulations, with internal metrics showing larger divergence from pre-unlearning states on the forget set and closer retention on the retain set compared to baselines.
llm-security.why_it_matters: Targets frequency-aware unlearning with automated retain/forget control, improving robustness to paraphrase/adversarial probes—relevant for red-teaming, safety fine-tuning, and deployment-time data governance.
llm-security.reason: Directly tackles unlearning/memorization—a core LLM security concern (data extraction, forgetting) with a practical adaptive method and measured leakage improvements.

llm-security.title: Proving the Utility of Large Language Models in Cybersecurity Simulations: A Comprehensive Examination
llm-security.summary: The paper evaluates LLMs for cybersecurity simulations, using YAML to represent complex network configurations and to drive pipelines that support RL agent training. It compares LLM-based techniques to classical methods like Double Q-learning with PER, claiming improved efficiency, adaptability, and realism in cyberattack simulations. In benchmarks on multiple synthetic topologies, LLM-instantiated Python agents reached up to a 94.5% compromise rate and 0.02–0.06s per assessment, a ~25,000x–50,000x speedup over traditional RL cycles.
llm-security.why_it_matters: Shows LLM-driven generation/execution pipelines can massively accelerate cyber-sim training and evaluation, relevant to secure LLM autonomy and sim-to-real robustness for time-series/agentic models.
llm-security.reason: Large-scale experimental evaluation of indirect prompt injection across channels and payloads maps closely to prompt-injection/jailbreak threat modeling and red-teaming methodology.

llm-security.title: Proof-of-Execution Memory: Defending LLM Agents Against Forged-Reasoning Attacks by Verifying What Actually Happened
llm-security.summary: The paper shows that FARMA-style forged-reasoning attacks bypass SENTINEL completely when the forgery is merely reworded by another LLM, with evasion on the first try and higher success on stronger models (98–100% on GPT-4o/4o-mini vs. 44% on Llama-3.1-8B). It introduces Proof-of-Execution Memory (PoEM), a tamper-evident HMAC-chained ledger that records only actually executed safety steps and gates skips on ledger confirmation, avoiding memory inspection. Across three models and three scenarios, PoEM reduces attack success to 0% with near-zero false positives, minimal overhead, robustness to attacks on itself, and works unchanged in a LangChain agent, while SENTINEL causes 33–50% false positives on legitimate operations.
llm-security.why_it_matters: It reframes agent safety from brittle content heuristics to verifiable execution traces, offering a practical, low-overhead control point that scales with model capability and integrates with common agent stacks.
llm-security.reason: Directly relevant to agentic LLM security: describes FARMA forged-reasoning attack on agent memory and a defenses' limitations (SENTINEL), matching interest in agent attack surfaces and red-teaming/guardrail bypass.
